output.summary: The yield decline is real: customer receiving rejects rose, and CMM gauge R&R, program, calibration and definitions were stable. The cause is unresolved. Three changes overlap in early August: the Corvane steel from 3 Aug, 12-hour shifts from 10 Aug, and deferred spindle service. The steady weekly decline fits a cumulative cause such as wear, but this is not established. The scrap-tag timestamps are batch-written, so they say nothing about fatigue. No evidence covers the new-operator cohort. A controlled A2-style test (staggered service, Tamsworth trial lots, cycle-counter match to CMM) separates the causes cheaply. Reverting shifts, cancelling the steel contract, disciplining operators or cutting inspection are premature or harmful.
